lit.\u0027% de cada elemento = (n átomos · m: "% of each element = (n atoms · atomic mass) / M × 100"
lit.\u0027¿Cuántos moles hay en 44 g de CO₂: "How many moles are there in 44 g of CO₂ (M = 44 g/mol)?"
lit.\u0027¿Qué contiene más átomos, 1 mol de: "Which contains more atoms, 1 mol of Fe or 1 mol of H₂?"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEn \u003cb\u003econdi:
"

Under standard conditions (0 °C and 1 atm) one mole of any ideal gas occupies 22.414 L. Thus V = n · 22.414 L. This does not apply to solids or liquids: their volume depends on density.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLa \u003cb\u003ecompo:
"

The percent composition by mass indicates what fraction of the molar mass each element contributes: % = (n · Ar) / M × 100. The sum is always 100%.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLa \u003cb\u003emasa:
"

The molar mass M of a substance is the mass of 1 mole of it. It is obtained by adding the atomic masses of all the atoms in the formula: M(H₂O) = 2·1.008 + 15.999 = 18.015 g/mol. Change the substance and see how the sum changes.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003ePara pasar de masa a:
"

To go from mass to moles, divide by M: n = m / M. To go from moles to particles, multiply by Avogadro’s number: N = n · NA. Move the mass and verify that moles and particles grow proportionally.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eUn \u003cb\u003emol\u:
"

A mole contains NA = 6.022 × 10²³ elementary entities. It is an enormous “package” that lets you count particles by weighing. Each sphere in the pile represents 10²² particles: with 60 spheres you have about one mole.

"
lit.\u0027«Sustancia» y «Masa»; la pestaña «: '“Substance” and “Mass”; the calculation tab converts grams → moles → particles step by step.'
lit.\u00271 mol = 6,022×10²³ entidades, sean: "1 mole = 6.022×10²³ entities, whether atoms, molecules or ions"
lit.\u00271 mol de átomos de carbono-12 pesa: "1 mole of carbon-12 atoms weighs 1 g"
lit.\u0027Aporte de cada elemento a la masa: "Contribution of each element to the molar mass."
lit.\u0027cada esfera representa 10²² partíc: 'each sphere stands for 10²² particles; the pile grows with the mass.'
lit.\u0027Compara 1 mol de dos sustancias: e: 'Compare 1 mol of two substances: the number of spheres is the same, the mass is not.'
lit.\u0027El volumen de 0,5 mol de gas ideal: "The volume of 0.5 mol of ideal gas at STP is…"
lit.\u0027Elige una sustancia y mueve la mas: "Choose a substance and move the mass: the pile of spheres shows how many particles there are (each = 10²²). In “Calculation” you see the step-by-step work."
lit.\u0027En CNTP (0 °C, 1 atm) 1 mol de gas: "At STP (0 °C, 1 atm) 1 mole of ideal gas occupies 22.4 L"
lit.\u0027Iguales en moléculas/átomos: 1 mol: "Equal in molecules/atoms: 1 mole of entities of each"
lit.\u0027La masa molar del agua (H = 1,008;: "The molar mass of water (H = 1.008; O = 15.999) is…"
lit.\u0027La masa molar es la suma de las ma: "Molar mass is the sum of the atomic masses of the formula, in g/mol"
lit.\u0027la molécula que gira es una entida: 'the rotating molecule is one entity of the chosen substance.'
lit.\u0027M se obtiene sumando masas atómica: "M is obtained by adding atomic masses."
lit.\u0027Pon 18,0 g de agua: ≈ 1 mol, unas: 'Set 18.0 g of water: ≈ 1 mol, about 60 spheres (6.0 × 10²³ molecules).'
lit.\u0027Revisa la composición del agua: ≈: 'Check the composition of water: ≈ 11 % H and 89 % O by mass.'
lit.\u0027Un mol es un número de entidades,: "A mole is a number of entities, not a mass."
